name: allocation-slider
title: Allocation slider
description: Split 100% between parts: draggable dividers on one bar, a number field per part, a lockable part and a total that must read 100.
docs: parts are { id, label } in the order they stand on the bar, and value is a record of what each holds, by id; onValueChange reports the whole record. total (default 100), step and min (the least any part may hold) set the rules, and unit is written after the numbers. The dividers between the parts are sliders in their own right: dragging one moves the share between the part on its left and the part on its right, so the total stays fixed, and its spoken value names both ("Email 40%, Social 35%"). Arrow keys move a step, Shift or the Page keys ten, Home and End to the least either part can hold. Each part also has a number field: typing a share takes the difference from the other free parts, or gives it to them, in proportion to what they hold, and the number is kept to what they can make room for. With lockable every part gets a lock. A locked part keeps its share, its field is read-only, and the dividers on its sides slide along with it while the free parts on either side trade between themselves (locked and defaultLocked, with onLockedChange, set the locks). The readout at the top says "Adds up to 100%", or what is missing or too much, and Balance spreads that over the free parts; data that does not add up shows its unassigned part in the bar. Parts are told apart by name and by a shade of grey, never by colour alone. Several dividers that stand on one spot (a part with nothing in it) are told apart by the way the pointer goes. The helpers in allocation-slider/shares.ts (evenShares, setShare, balance) work without the component.
